# We're bringing on our first RevOps lead at Stuut, and I've been careful not to frame the role as a typical GTM engineer. · 2026-06-23T00:00:00+00:00

We're bringing on our first RevOps lead at Stuut, and I've been careful not to frame the role as a typical GTM engineer.

Clay popularized the term a few years ago, and it caught on quickly. But I think it has also created more confusion than clarity. A great GTME can build workflows, clean up data, enrich accounts, automate outbound motions, and make the sales team faster. While that's useful, it's not the same thing as what a strong RevOps function actually does at a scaling company.

RevOps is the conductor of all the parts of a revenue motion simultaneously: sales, marketing, partnerships, customer expansion, and everything in between. In that sense, it's really GTM Ops. It should sit in finance because the job is not just to make these teams more efficient, but also to connect go-to-market activity to the business's financial reality.
